abstract: In Escherichia coli, SeqA-mediated cohesion at snap loci on the right replichore persists longer, but its role in DNA double-strand break (DSB) repair remains untested. Here, we show that site-specific DSBs at snap loci confer higher cell survival than nonsnap loci. With perturbations affecting sister cohesion [ΔseqA, topoisomerase IV overexpression (T4-OE)], this survival advantage was progressively reduced, with the combined ΔseqA T4-OE strain retaining only a transient advantage. The increased survival correlates with faster repair, reflected by rapid restoration of locus copy number and shorter-lived, thinner RecA-green fluorescent protein filaments. Consistent with more accurate repair, snap loci exhibited lower mutation accumulation under normal and antibiotic stress conditions. Comparative genome analysis of E. coli strains revealed higher GATC motif counts and higher sequence conservation. Together, these findings suggest that the chromosomal organization associated with prolonged sister cohesion at snap loci promotes efficient homologous recombination-mediated DSB repair and contributes to genome conservation.
